title: A recent visit with Duke and Mercer Ellington
summary: He recounts sitting in with Duke's band and probably seeing Duke for the last time.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: was like last week or the week before last. I saw Mercer. Mercer. He said—Mercer, said 'When are you coming on down to see me?' I said well, I happened to have 3 or 4 days off and I went by and caught it. I enjoyed it. It brought back a lot of memories, especially with Duke and myself.

But, I played with Duke. Duke came up here to do the track, and he was up here for a week. He stayed here at the hotel. And when I went out there, when he say me walking up toward the band, he started playing "Tuxedo Junction". And Mercer was playing trumpet in the band. And he got up there, he stopped. I said, "Mercer, give me that trumpet." Hand it to me (inaudible) while we was playing "Tuxedo Junction". Just a little get together in a place like that, you know. And then, I saw him at that night. (inaudible).
Before you start the next one, I don't want to go to that. [PAUSE]
Well, after finishing that, Duke here at the Concorde came back, He had to (inaudible), and we talked
about him. And then, he didn't come downstairs. He went up to the room because he wanted to go rest. And, Duke really loved steaks. He wanted to get him a big steak.
And then, I think that was the last time I saw Duke before he left us, you know. He was a beautiful man.
Yeah. He had a very long and very fruitful career.
